text:
Asha: Heads up — I have a 9-hour layover in SFO before heading to the offsite. Anyone have recs for how to survive a long layover? Lounge access vs airport hotel vs exploring the city? Also worried about carry-on naps and showering.

Ben: If you have a Priority Pass or certain credit cards, lounges + shower is life-changing. Food, plugs, quiet corners. Otherwise, consider booking a day room at an airport hotel if you need real sleep.

lounge-bot: quick-options: Priority Pass lounges at SFO: Club at SJC (if eligible), Plaza Premium in T3, some contract lounges require same-day boarding pass. Shower availability varies; call ahead.

Ravi: For a 9h layover I'd do a short city hop only if transit time <90m each way. Otherwise lounge + walk the terminals. Bring a small quick-dry blanket, inflatable neck pillow, and earplugs.

Clara: Shower tip: bring a tiny foldable towel and a travel-sized deodorant in carry-on. Some lounges provide towels but not all. Also pack a toothbrush kit for freshening up before the next flight.

Sam: Food/snack hack: pack a few protein bars, one resealable fruit cup, and an empty water bottle to refill at a fountain after security. Airport coffee is overpriced; bring instant coffee packets if you care.

Asha: Anyone used the minute or hour-based rooms (like Minute Suites or Aerotel)? Worth it for naps?

Ben: Minute Suites are great for a proper nap+power nap equipment. Book early — they sell out. They have a daybed, privacy curtain, outlet, sometimes a small desk. Good if you need 2-4h of real rest.

Ravi: If you want to explore, keep luggage in left-luggage or use an airport locker/service. Also check transit visa rules if leaving the airport internationally.

Clara: Seat strategy: pick a seat near the gate you depart from and a power outlet. If sleeping in the gate area, an empty row near the windows is usually quieter. Gate areas by food courts are loud.

lounge-bot: checklist: passport, boarding pass, lounge pass/credit card, refillable bottle, toothbrush kit, earplugs, light blanket, chargers, meds. Note: some lounges require same-day boarding pass + partner network rules.

Sam: Also, if you need a shower but no lounge access, some terminals have paid shower stalls or adjacent hotels with walk-in spa access. Book via app (Snooze or LoungeBuddy) to check availability.

Asha: Great — leaning lounge + short nap in a minute suite if affordable. Quick poll: reply "lounge" if you'd pick lounge, "dayroom" if you'd book a day hotel, "explore" if you'd leave the airport for the city. Also any tips for staying hydrated on long layovers?

Ben: Hydration = water + electrolyte sachet. Avoid too much coffee/alcohol. Eat something salty + protein to avoid crash.

Ravi: Pro tip: set a phone alarm and multiple gentle alarms 30m before boarding to avoid missing the flight after a deep nap.

Clara: If you're flying with company kit and worried about leaving it unattended, ask ops if an approved colleague can watch it at the gate or use a locker. Don't check critical gear.

Asha: Thanks! Voting now. :)
